title: Workload-slice-driven profile assembler for model onboarding and pinning
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Goal: Build a harness component that assembles performance profiles per model+version by slicing real workload surfaces (traffic buckets, prompt families, sequence length distributions) and driving eval runners across those slices. The assembled profile artifacts will be compatible with the existing profile publisher, enable deterministic version pinning heuristics, and provide explainable delta metrics for rollout decisions.

Scope / Acceptance Criteria:
- Ingest lightweight workload manifests (traffic-slice descriptors) and map to sampling strategies (prefix-preserve, tail-heavy, long-seq bags).
- Produce deterministic dataset shards and associated prompt variants for each slice (stable seed + schema metadata).
- Execute eval runners in parallel across slices and aggregate per-token latency, p95/p99, token-throughput, and quality regressions into a single profile artifact.
- Output profile artifact that the profile publisher can consume and that contains explicit pinning recommendations (preferred quantization, kernel options, fallback variant).
- Provide an opt-in mode to attach recent production traces (redacted) to weight slices for weighted aggregation.

Progress updates / decisions so far:
- 2025-11-11 (Aisha): Spike completed to validate deterministic shard generation using composite seed (model+version+slice-id). Proof-of-concept repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness/pull/312 (WIP).
- 2025-11-12 (Mateo): Decided to reuse existing eval runner contract but add an execution_hint field ("slice_id","preserve_prefix"). This avoids forking runners and keeps backward compat.
- 2025-11-14 (Aisha): Trade-off discussion: embedding production trace attachments increases fidelity but expands PII/redaction burden. Chose opt-in trace attachments gated by security_review_required flag.
- 2025-11-16 (Mateo): Implemented sampling strategies: uniform-by-prompt, length-stratified, and tail-sampling. Unit tests cover seeding determinism. PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness/pull/319
- 2025-11-18 (Design review): Requested changes to profile schema to include human-readable slice_descriptions and coverage_metrics. Design notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Profile+Assembler+Design
- 2025-11-19 (Eng sync): Agreed to publish an interim profile format (v0.9) to unblock rollouts, with a migration path to v1.0 after telemetry validation.

Open tasks / next steps:
- Finish PR #319 (integration tests with harness CI) and address flaky failures in the length-stratified sampler.
- Add an opt-in dashboard tile in Console for slice-level metrics (latency histogram + weight contribution). Wire to metrics: dashboards/bench-profiles/slices (Ticket: PM-812).
- Coordinate with security for trace-attachment gating (ENG-44012 dependency).
- Finish profile publisher adapter for v0.9 artifacts and add pin recommendation heuristics (ENG-41800 dependency).

Review feedback and follow-ups:
- Performance team (K. O'Connor): request to include KV-cache hit ratio estimate per slice; added as a non-blocking follow-up (will be in v1.0).
- PM (L. Chen): prioritize providing a simple human summary in the profile artifact ("recommended_pin_reason"). Added to schema changes.
- QA: create fuzz tests for sampler edge-cases (very-short, very-long sequences). Estimated 2 points.

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: Non-deterministic sampling could create flaky comparisons across profile generations. Mitigation: use composite seeding and record full sampler seed in artifact metadata.
- Risk: Large trace attachments increase storage and cost. Mitigation: sample with weight threshold and compress traces; require opt-in.

Links to artifacts and references:

- Spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/bench-harness/pull/312 (WIP)

Notes for on-call / incidents: If a profile run shows >20% p99 regression after pinning, auto-abort rollout and open ENG-incident-XXXXX; keep profile artifacts for post-mortem.
